{{Short description|Indian urban activist and author}}
'''Sathya Sankaran''' is an Indian urban technologist, civic activist, and author
based in [[Bengaluru]]. He is known for leading the decade-long citizen campaign
for [[Bengaluru Suburban Railway|Bengaluru's suburban rail]], serving as the first
Bicycle Mayor of Bengaluru (2018–2020), and founding [[Urban Morph]], a sustainable
mobility consultancy.

== Career ==
Sankaran holds a degree in Computer Science and a postgraduate qualification in
Public Policy.<ref name="bycs">{{cite web |url=https://bycs.org/bicycle-mayor/sathya-sankaran/
|title=Sathya Sankaran – Bicycle Mayor |publisher=BYCS |access-date=2026-03-08}}</ref>
He worked in the technology sector for over 20 years before transitioning to
urban activism and mobility consulting.

=== Namma Railu campaign ===
From 2009 to 2020, Sankaran was a founding member of the Namma Railu (Our Train)
campaign, a citizen-led effort to bring suburban rail to Bengaluru through the
online platform [[Praja.in]].<ref name="greenpeace">{{cite web
|url=https://www.greenpeace.org/india/en/story/10816/bengalurus-steelflyoverbeda-activist-talks-sustainable-mobility/
|title=Bengaluru's #SteelFlyoverBeda activist talks sustainable mobility
|publisher=Greenpeace India |year=2017}}</ref> The campaign involved coalition-building
across 39 citizen organizations, technical research, and sustained engagement with
state and federal government.<ref name="tnm-modalu">{{cite web
|url=https://www.thenewsminute.com/article/first-we-want-trains-b-luru-citizen-activists-launch-campaign-suburban-rail-87124
|title=First we want trains: Bengaluru citizen activists launch campaign for suburban rail
|publisher=The News Minute |date=30 August 2018}}</ref> The Union Cabinet approved
the Bengaluru Suburban Rail project in October 2020.<ref name="ie-suburban">{{cite web
|url=https://indianexpress.com/article/cities/bangalore/from-december-7-suburban-trains-to-run-in-all-four-directions-from-bengaluru-7091131/
|title=From December 7, suburban trains to run in all four directions from Bengaluru
|publisher=Indian Express |date=5 December 2020}}</ref>

Sankaran documented this campaign in his 2026 book ''Break the Block: Twelve
Lessons for Citizen-Led Change from Bengaluru's Rail Campaign''.
<ref name="book">{{cite book |last=Sankaran |first=Sathya
|title=Break the Block: Twelve Lessons for Citizen-Led Change from Bengaluru's
Rail Campaign |year=2026 |publisher=Notion Press |isbn=979-8-90269-374-1}}</ref>

=== Bicycle Mayor ===
In May 2018, Sankaran was appointed Bengaluru's first Bicycle Mayor by the
Amsterdam-based organization BYCS.<ref name="hindu-bm">{{cite web
|url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/cities/bangalore/bengaluru-gets-its-first-bicycle-mayor/article23952757.ece
|title=Bengaluru gets its first 'Bicycle Mayor' |publisher=The Hindu
|date=22 May 2018}}</ref><ref name="national">{{cite web
|url=https://www.thenationalnews.com/world/asia/bicycle-mayor-faces-an-uphill-task-in-bengaluru-1.734197
|title='Bicycle mayor' faces an uphill task in Bengaluru
|publisher=The National |date=6 July 2021}}</ref> He served in the role
until 2020, advocating for cycling infrastructure and non-motorised transport policy.

=== Relief Riders ===
During the [[COVID-19 pandemic in India|COVID-19 pandemic]] in 2020, Sankaran
co-founded Relief Riders, a volunteer cyclist network that delivered essential
supplies across Bengaluru.<ref name="cm-relief">{{cite web
|url=https://citizenmatters.in/bengaluru-relief-riders-cyclists-home-delivery-essentials-medicines-to-senior-citizens/
|title=Bengaluru Relief Riders: Cyclists home-deliver essentials, medicines to senior citizens
|publisher=Citizen Matters |year=2020 |access-date=2026-03-08}}</ref> The initiative received a
[[Nobel Peace Prize]] nomination in 2022 and the [[United Nations]] World
Bicycle Day Special Award in 2021.

=== Urban Morph ===
Sankaran founded Urban Morph, a sustainable mobility consultancy based in
Bengaluru. The firm's projects include Altmo (a mobility intelligence platform),
Church Street First (India's pioneering pedestrianisation initiative, which won
the Urban Mobility India 2021 Commendation Award and Volvo Innovation Awards 2021),
and Pedaluru (a campaign to transform Bengaluru into India's cycling capital).
<ref name="dh-coe">{{cite web
|url=https://www.deccanherald.com/india/karnataka/bengaluru/cycling-in-the-city-whats-the-way-forward-3067843
|title=Cycling in Bengaluru: What's the way forward?
|publisher=Deccan Herald |date=14 June 2024}}</ref>
In September 2024, Urban Morph partnered with the [[Indian Institute of Science]]
to establish India's first Centre of Excellence for Active Mobility.

== Awards ==
* UN World Bicycle Day Special Award (2021)
* Nobel Peace Prize nomination (Relief Riders, 2022)
* Urban Mobility India Commendation Award (Church Street First, 2021)
* Volvo Innovation Awards (2021)
